extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of sociology/social theory; scholars interested in class, leisure, and cultural analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and analyzes the characteristic aptitudes, propensities, and social processes that define the leisure class versus industrial classes, and the modern survivals of predatory/prowess traits (e.g., sports, dueling, martial spirit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dominant traits of the early barbarian leisure class
rubrics_metrics.description: The dominant traits of the early barbarian leisure class were bold aggression, an alert sense of status, and a free resort to fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members held their place by tenure of prowess; in later barbarian culture aggression gave place to shrewd practice and chicanery. These traits survive as 'aristocratic virtues' alongside pecuniary virtues such as providence, prudence, and chicanery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for admission to the leisure class
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission to the class is gained by exercise of the pecuniary aptitudes—aptitudes for acquisition rather than for serviceability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ground of selection has shifted so modern admission depends chiefly on pecuniary aptitudes; selection conserves aptitudes effective for pecuniary ends rather than original predatory prowess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenacity of purpose / consistency of aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenacity of purpose or consistency of aim is a remaining predatory trait distinguishing successful predatory barbarians and present successful individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This trait also appears in industrial classes due to training; it therefore does not by itself uniquely mark the leisure class but distinguishes both from shiftless dependents and lower-class delinquents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinship between pecuniary man and delinquent temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal pecuniary man is like the ideal delinquent in his unscrupulous conversion of goods and persons to his own ends and in a callous disregard of others and of remoter effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They differ in that the pecuniary man has a keener sense of status and works more consistently and farsightedly toward ends. Shared traits include proclivity to 'sport,' gambling, and aimless emulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pecuniary vs industrial ranges of aptitudes and propensities
rubrics_metrics.description: Two divergent lines of development: the pecuniary (personal, invidious, qualitative/status-oriented) and the industrial (impersonal, non-invidious, quantitative/sequence/use-oriented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pecuniary employments conserve the personal/qualitative bent; industrial employments conserve the impersonal/quantitative bent. Each is a multiform expression of a given temperamental variant and selection acts to conserve the aptitudes appropriate to each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure-class life conserves archaic/barbarian temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: The leisure-class life and scheme of life should further the conservation of the barbarian temperament—chiefly the quasi-peaceable (bourgeois) variant and to some extent the predatory variant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of disturbances a difference of temperament between classes should be traceable: aristocratic/bourgeois virtues among upper classes, industrial virtues among mechanically industrious classes. However, the test is not conclusive due to multiple intervening factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial life requires impersonal, non-invidious interest (industrial virtues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern industry requires an impersonal, non-invidious interest in the work in hand; without this, elaborate industrial processes would be impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spiritual aptitude for work differentiates the workman from the criminal and the captain of industry; selection favors this aptitude in certain occupations, limiting the dominance of pure pecuniary temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescriptive transmission of leisure-class traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescriptive position of the leisure class as exemplar of reputability imposes many leisure-class features upon lower classes via precept and example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic servants and contact with masters transmit upper-class notions of good and beautiful, disseminating aristocratic traits across society ('Like master, like man'). This mitigates class differences in temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic pressure and underfeeding produce pecuniary traits in lower classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The pecuniary struggle produces an underfed class, leading to a closely enforced struggle for daily means and a narrowing of effort to invidious self-assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This causes industrial traits to obsolesce through disuse among the poor, indirectly assimilating lower classes to upper-class pecuniary types and conserving pecuniary traits in the population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure class conserves traits and retards industrial adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution of a leisure class conserves and fortifies traditions of the archaic regime, increasing the chances of survival of barbarian traits both within and outside the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms: (1) direct transmission by inheritance/transfusion of leisure-class blood, (2) conservation of traditions and prescriptive schemes of life—resulting in lowered industrial efficiency for the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Martial spirit as a leisure-class trait
rubrics_metrics.description: The hereditarily leisure class is endowed with the fighting propensity or 'martial spirit' to a higher degree than the middle classes; warlike prowess is honorific and admired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The upper class claims pride in warlike enthusiasm; government as an ostensible upper-class occupation has predatory origins. Lower-class delinquents may share this spirit; industrial classes are relatively apathetic except under special provocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duel as a leisure-class institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The duel is in substance a resort to fight as a final settlement of difference of opinion and prevails normally only where there is an hereditary leisure class and almost exclusively among that class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) military/naval officers (usually leisure class by status and training), and (2) lower-class delinquents. The duel shades into unprovoked private fights as social obligations of reputability among certain classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boyhood predaceous interval as reversion to archaic temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Boys commonly pass through a predaceous interval characterized by initiative, aggressive self-assertion, isolation of interests, and less sensibility to rebuke—reproducing an earlier predatory human phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Girls less commonly undergo this interval. Failure to transition fully to adult (industrial) temperament results in adult persistence of fighting temper and arrested spiritual development; schoolboys' disturbances reproduce this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports as manifestations of predatory exploit and make-believe
rubrics_metrics.description: Sports (prize-fights, bull-fights, athletics, shooting, angling, yachting, games of skill) are classed as exploits—partly emulative ferocity and partly deliberate repute-seeking—and are expressive of an archaic predatory temperament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sports exhibit a large element of make-believe and histrionic exaggeration; ostensible motives (love of nature, recreation) are often subsidiary covers. Sports keep nature desolated (killing wildlife) despite claims of nature-love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure-class canon of decorum: conspicuous waste and strict futility
rubrics_metrics.description: The canons of reputable living exclude from the leisure-class scheme of life all activity that cannot be classed as conspicuous leisure; they demand strict and comprehensive futility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescriptive exclusion makes sports and similar activities the only decorous outdoor occupations, and it tends to eliminate substantially useful or purposeful modes of action from accredited life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual functional requirement for sports to be sustained
rubrics_metrics.description: For an employment to hold place as decorous recreation it must meet two requirements: (1) the leisure-class requirement of ulterior futility (conspicuous waste) and (2) the instinct-of-workmanship requirement of proximate purposefulness (dexterous/emulative exertion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sports satisfy both by providing a colorable pretense of purpose while remaining essentially futile, reconciling the individual's organic trend toward purposeful action with the leisure-class demand for decorous waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of occupational slang as evidence of make-believe and group membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a special slang in any employment is probably evidence that the occupation is substantially make-believe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slang often borrows sanguinary locutions from warfare; special slang serves as secret communication but also signals the histrionic/narrative nature of the activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social encouragement of pseudo-military organizations and athletics fosters predatory traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fostering of 'boys' brigades', college spirit, and college athletics by clergymen and pillars of society encourages predatory, martial, or prestidigitation habits among youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such encouragement helps perpetuate the predatory temperament into new generations by institutionalizing make-believe military discipline and fostering habits of ferocity and emulative exploit.
